# Google Lens

*Product* · also written Lens

Google's visual search: search with a photo or a part of the screen instead of typed words.

**Glossary** (*Google Lens*): Google's visual search, which Google said it built after seeing young users upload pictures and expect answers about them; more than 1.5 billion people use it every month, according to Google's May 2025 announcement.

8 claims mention it: 1 from Google's documentation, 5 shown or said at the event (1 not in Google docs, 2 confirmed by Google docs, 1 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Search with Google Lens in Chrome](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/15086890?hl=en), [Search with an image on Google](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/1325808?hl=en).

- [`D1-C191`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Docs: Google's May 2025 Search announcement says more than 1.5 billion people use Google Lens to search what they see every month. `[D1-C191, docs, Google blog (20 May 2025), https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/google-search-ai-mode-update/]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C188`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: Google said it noticed young users uploading pictures to reverse image search and expecting results that answer something about the picture, and that Google Lens was its answer to that behaviour. `[D1-C188, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C190`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google said Google Lens is used by over 1.5 billion people (figure as said on stage on 30 September 2026; no period was given). `[D1-C190, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D3-C458`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Multimodal searches reported in Search Console include searches with Google Lens, Circle to Search on Android, images uploaded to Google Search and Chrome's right-click search on an image. `[D3-C458, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C460`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: In a live demo, Google Lens on an Android phone identified a photographed object and listed websites selling it, with deep links that allow buying it online. `[D3-C460, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C159`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: The keynote's personal favourites in the evolution of Search were Google Translate, voice search, the Knowledge Graph (relating entities to give context) and Google Lens. `[D1-C159, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C200`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Analysis: Visual search predates transformers in Google's own history: its Search timeline dates Google Images to 2001 and Google Lens to 2017, the year Google Research published the Transformer, so read the stage remark as being about today's multimodal AI search. `[D1-C200, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C462`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Analysis: Google's Performance report help says the queries dimension is not available for the multimodal search type, because these searches mostly use images, so judge image-led traffic by page, country and device, and make product and article images distinctive enough for Lens to match. `[D3-C462, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
